summary: inventory-api is running as a persistent systemd service on node1 and remained available while the kernel OOM-killed the memory hog. It recovered successfully after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated unprivileged inventory-api account and HTTP service on port 8080.
Enabled automatic startup/restart with OOMScoreAdjust=-900, MemoryMin=32M, and MemoryLow=64M.
Ran a contained memory-pressure test with the hog at OOMScoreAdjust=1000; the kernel killed the hog at its 192 MiB limit.
Verified inventory-api stayed healthy with the same PID and zero restarts during the OOM event.
Rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and inventory-api recovered with its protection settings and data intact.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is a managed, OOM-protected service
evidence.summary: The service is enabled and active, listens on port 8080, serves health and inventory JSON, restarts automatically, and its live process has oom_score_adj=-900.

evidence.requirement: The memory hog is stopped by the kernel while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: The hog ran with oom_score_adj=1000. Kernel logs identify its PID as the OOM victim and systemd reports result=oom-kill; inventory-api remained active, responsive, and had zero restarts.

Pre-restart boot ID and healthy data were captured, the reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed from 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146 to aafdcc3d-f477-41e7-8757-995d2b2dbabe, and the enabled service returned healthy inventory data afterward with oom_score_adj=-900.
